clue.text: Turn round here to give a lift? Blow the girl!

definitions.text: Turn round here to give a lift?

parts.note: to blow is to wind, as a gale does
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in annoyance at a girl while turning round to give her a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch with a drum that is cranked round to haul up loads is exactly something turned round to lift.

clue.text: One may be gripped by Nelson's achievement

definitions.text: One may be gripped by Nelson's achievement

parts.words: One may be gripped by Nelson's achievement
parts.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold, so someone grappled in one is a fighter on the mat rather than an admiral's triumph

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson's great victory had a firm grip on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson suggests the admiral, but a half or full nelson is a hold in wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappling sportsmen are the people who get caught in a nelson hold.

clue.text: Rotten centre in a fruit

indicators.note: rotten suggests something decayed and fallen apart, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit has gone bad in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' rearranges CENTREINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Fine examples of ormolu, lustrous to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gilded ormolu pieces shine somewhat, making fine examples.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is slang for a remarkable or outstanding specimen of something.

clue.text: Bow when hauled in by NCO, in attempt at humour?

indicators.note: being hauled in by someone means being pulled inside, so these pieces sit within the officer's letters

parts.note: SM, sergeant major, is a non-commissioned officer
a bow is a curve, an arc
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A sergeant drags someone in for a bow, perhaps as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests a polite bend; here it is a curve. SM, sergeant major, is the usual crossword NCO, and 'hauled in by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking irony is a form of wit, hence the question mark on humour.

clue.text: Point debatable — hard to iron out

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
a moot point is one open to debate
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A disputed issue proves difficult to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten creases or difficulties is to make level, the verb sense.

clue.text: Unlikely character perhaps had some substance, outwardly

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the substance word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: matter is physical substance

indicators.note: unlikely here works as a sign that the letters of the word had come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: An improbable figure seemed to have some real depth on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal, giving ADH; 'outwardly' signals the container, and 'some' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea-party host in Alice in Wonderland is a famous fictional figure, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Alternatively, cut the deck

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Someone offers to cut the pack of cards instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cards, but the definition is a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship the lowest deck is called by this name.

clue.text: Old yen' died, stifled by female, once a lively one

indicators.note: being stifled by something means being smothered inside it, so these letters go within the female

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, yen
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An old man's yearning died, smothered by a woman who was once spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' hints that the word is dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a boisterous, high-spirited girl, an old-fashioned term.

clue.text: Excellent! B marvellous!

parts.note: super is a colloquial word for marvellous

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic exclamation praising something rated B.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an exclamation of high praise, meaning outstanding.

clue.text: Have great success by forty, on radio?

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so the letters are what the word sounds like

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone makes it big by the age of forty, broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word; the Roman numerals said aloud give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine others or do outstandingly well is to triumph.

clue.text: Sing-song and a few drinks, around university?

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

indicators.note: around here means turned about, so the university's name is read backwards

parts.note: Yale is a famous American university

explanation.surface: Students gather for a singsong and drinks near the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives ELAY; the university is the American one in New Haven, Connecticut.
explanation.definitionFit: A short song with a refrain repeated, often sung by a group, is a simple song.

clue.text: Change one's expression, rant wildly, and criticise

indicators.note: wildly suggests letters flung about at random, so the word rant is rearranged

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone changes their face, raves furiously and lashes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges RANT into TRAN; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To render words into another language is to change how something is expressed.

clue.text: Adam's follower is big in New York

definitions.meaning: the word that follows Adam's in the name of the throat lump
New York is nicknamed the Big followed by this fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit names both the larynx bump and New York's nickname.

clue.text: Overindulge in backing horse, evoking pithy comment?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
backing means going backwards, so the horse word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
to pig is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Gorging while betting on a horse provokes a sharp remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives ERAM and 'in' signals the container; 'evoking' is a link word, and 'horse' wants to be the animal ridden, not bet on.
explanation.definitionFit: A short witty saying is a terse, clever remark.

clue.text: High bridge among outstanding features?

parts.note: the bridge here is that of the nose, high and prominent on the face rather than a structure over a river

explanation.surface: A lofty bridge stands among remarkable landmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge and features suggest architecture or landscape, but they are parts of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose with a prominent high bridge, as on classical busts, sticks out on the face.

clue.text: Secure clothes in fashion, however, at first

indicators.note: at first says the however word comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: but means however
the ton is old-fashioned for high fashion or society

explanation.surface: Keep clothes stylish but only at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as a noun in the surface but belongs to the definition as an object; 'at first' fixes the order and 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten a coat or shirt by its small discs is to do it up.

clue.text: Studiously avoid capsizing vehicles in French river

indicators.note: in places the reversed vehicles inside the river

parts.note: the Oise is a river in northern France

indicators.note: capsizing means turning over, so the vehicles word is turned round

parts.note: carts are vehicles

explanation.surface: Drivers steer clear of overturning their cars in a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' gives STRAC and 'in' signals the container; the river joins the Seine below Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude someone from society is to shun them deliberately.

clue.text: One's output is all very fine, but essentially unreadable

definitions.text: One's output is all very fine, but essentially unreadable

parts.words: One's output is all very fine, but essentially unreadable
parts.note: a machine for destroying documents produces fine strips of paper that can no longer be read

explanation.surface: A writer's work is very polished but basically illegible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all very fine' seems to praise a writer; it means cut into fine strips.
explanation.definitionFit: An office machine slices paper into thin strips that cannot be read.

clue.text: Favourite type of wood inlaid for part of fittings

indicators.note: inlaid means set into a surface, so the wood goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
elm is a type of wood

explanation.surface: A favoured kind of timber is inlaid in some furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelmet is a board or valance concealing curtain rails, one of a room's furnishings.

clue.text: Put up with crew seeing Tracy in the 'papers?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: taken as written
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A reader has to tolerate the crew of a newspaper reporting on someone called Tracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. Tracy Tupman is a member of the club in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracy is the first name of one of Mr Pickwick's companions in the Dickens novel.

clue.text: OK, what are you up to?

definitions.text: OK, what are you up to?

parts.words: OK, what are you up to?
parts.note: being OK or satisfactory is being up to a certain standard, the starting line in the idiom

explanation.surface: Someone asks a friend what they are getting up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The question sounds like a casual enquiry; it is the idiom 'up to ...' meaning satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are good enough you are said to be up to this mark, the idiom for acceptable.

clue.text: Outrageous cost: to secure this breed

indicators.note: outrageous suggests something wildly out of order, so the letters of cost are rearranged

parts.note: to secure something is to tie it

explanation.surface: Buying this dog breed costs a ridiculous amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outrageous' rearranges COST into SCOT; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aberdeen terrier is a dog breed with a short nickname.

clue.text: Became less quiet, having a row

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a rank is a row, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: A room grew noisier as an argument broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel; it is a line. 'having a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking is getting smaller, so the past tense means diminished.

clue.text: Being in error, perhaps?

parts.note: the proverb says to err is natural to people, so a creature who errs is one of us

explanation.surface: Someone may be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Recalls the proverb 'To err is human, to forgive divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a mortal being, and mistakes are proverbially part of our nature.

clue.text: Paid to get books in for composition

indicators.note: in places the books inside the paid word

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone is paid to bring in books for an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A short polyphonic choral piece is a musical work.

clue.text: Sport involved speed — flat out

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of sport are rearranged

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: The sport demanded pace, so competitors went at full tilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SPORT into PROST. 'flat out' suggests full speed but means lying face down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying stretched out face down is being flat on the ground.

clue.text: One involved in jazz society

indicators.note: involved in means taken inside, so the one goes into the jazz word

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a jazz club.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese secret criminal society.

clue.text: High-flier given a bit of support about following article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the support piece goes round the other letters

parts.note: a strut is a structural support
on means following, as in 'from that day on'
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ambitious person is given a little help with the article that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link word, and 'about' signals the container; 'High-flier' sounds like an ambitious person but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller literally flies higher than anyone.

clue.text: One needs government backing the old, old story

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the government word is read in reverse

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A person needs a government that supports the elderly, the same old tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link word; 'backing' turns DAIL into LIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is an ancient tale.

clue.text: Rig clear round for little Tom

parts.note: a rig or outfit is a kit

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the clear word is reversed

parts.note: net means clear, as in clear profit after deductions

explanation.surface: A horse clears a round in show-jumping gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' gives TEN; 'for' is a link word, and 'Tom' is the male cat, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, so a young one is a baby cat.

clue.text: Had eager spin bowler?

indicators.note: spin means a turning about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eager cricketer bowled spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' rearranges HADEAGER. The cricket suggestion misleads: a bowler is a hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is an example of something worn on the head.
